name: Runner Extras - Integer Virtual Table Window
brief: Issues #2350, #3376, #3438 and #3485: the Integer system virtual table (2000000026) is computed on demand on the service tier by IntegerDataProvider, which clamps every request to [-1000000000..1000000000]. Since #3485 the runner serves it from that same provider, so no row is materialised. This suite pins the runner-specific remainder: that the 500,000-row cap and the [-1000..100000] base window a materialised store forced are gone from every request path.
description: What the Integer table itself answers - that Number 0, negatives, 250000 and -250000 are real rows, that a range filter yields every value in order, that a multi-range filter yields the union of its ranges - is plain BC behaviour and is covered upstream in the al-language corpus (Test Integer Virtual Table, codeunit 60368). This suite deliberately asserts none of it exactly. Each arm asserts a LOWER BOUND past a number the runner used to impose: a count above the old 500,000-row cap, a last row above the old base window's upper edge 100000, a keyed Get at 999999999. Plus the one invariant changing the row source could have broken: a temporary Record Integer still holds only what AL inserted (#2524).
